note: Seed blocks declared by an artifact but never spent. The freshness scan skips the artifacts it is told to allow, so a block declared inside an allow-listed artifact is invisible to it; these reservations are checked separately by benchmarks.a1_seed_reservations and by the two-path preflight.

shared_blocks.label: the six historical audit seeds at cap 112
shared_blocks.basis: the construct preregistration's gate C9_comparator_row requires each cell to reproduce the cap-112 comparator row for its seed, so the two designs must run the same six seeds; both artifacts declare the reuse in seed_reuse and pair it against the 0.14.0 audit

shared_blocks.label: the cap-112 baseline-availability block, adopted by the two-path manifest
shared_blocks.basis: A1-BASELINE-AVAILABILITY-1 ran these six seeds at caps 112 and 64 and its per-seed rows are recorded; A1-TWO-PATH-1 declares the same six at cap 40 as a PROVISIONAL CANDIDATE block, so the manifest is not a fresh block. The manifest's own freshness field reads 'seed_collisions over docs JSON is empty at manifest time', which is true only because the scan skips its own allow list, of which the baseline-availability artifact is one.
shared_blocks.pending: whether the two-path manifest keeps the spent baseline block or fixes a fresh one is the owner's decision, not a guard's; until it is made, this block is recorded as reused rather than fresh.
